A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 19-page versions of the same VGPO paper, including Appendices A-E. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original benchmark results, ablations, training dynamics, attention-correlation analysis and failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and analyses reported in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Visual Focus Score, gated linear Visual Attention Compensation, and intra- and inter-trajectory advantage reweighting. The algorithm and objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ViRL39K, Geo3K and MMK12 and evaluate the same ten mathematical/geometric and vision-dependent benchmarks. Appendix task and scenario coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: The main and appendix comparisons retain the same comparator memberships, including GRPO/DAPO, the six 7B reasoning baselines, and entropy/KL advantage-shaping methods. Updated citation years refer to the same evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Table 7 and the appendix experiments retain the same model configurations, sample counts, training budgets, batch settings, metrics and evaluation temperature of 0.0.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices B, C and E retain the same component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, compensation comparisons, weaker-model analysis, attention correlation and failure cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Appendix C's Pearson-correlation procedure. Neither version reports repeated-run/seed summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical table entries, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains VGPO's 66.6% mathematical and 63.3% vision-dependent averages, and Appendix C retains the correlation of approximately 0.67.

T1.justification: Equations 1-12 and their mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about intrinsic visual localization, mitigating temporal visual forgetting, dual-grained optimization and superior reasoning performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same mechanism interpretations and limitations concerning heuristic compensation and dependence on the visual encoder's representations. Appendix E's explanations of perceptual and logical failures are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 7, Appendix B.7 and Appendix C retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, prompt template and hidden-state implementation details. The code-release statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ji et al. (2025), 'Tree search for LLM agent reinforcement learning,' to the introduction and bibliography. Other bibliographic revisions concern existing works, and VGPO's substantive positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits mainly update citation years, author suffixes and bibliography metadata, including completing the GeoMath year and MathVerse title. The introduction drops 'emerging'; section organization and scientific exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Citation updates alter several captions, and bibliography and paragraph text reflow slightly. Figure graphics, table structures, axes and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds one background citation and refreshes references while preserving the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations. Some references become more complete, including GeoMath's year and MathVerse's title, while Qwen2.5-VL's full arXiv identifier becomes a less specific locator. These limited bibliographic tradeoffs do not produce a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
